name: Terbutaline

card.summary: A prescription beta-2 agonist for asthma with an FDA boxed warning against use in preterm labour; no appearance trials exist.
card.note: Boxed warning: oral terbutaline not approved for tocolysis; serious maternal heart events and deaths reported.

quick.overview:
Terbutaline is a beta-2 adrenergic agonist bronchodilator used as a reliever for asthma and reversible airway disease. It is available as tablets and injection and, outside the US, as an inhaler.

It appears in appearance discussion only as a member of the beta-2 agonist family. The sources reviewed do not document its use for fat loss or muscle and contain no trials for that purpose.
quick.mechanism: It selectively stimulates beta-2 receptors, raising cAMP and relaxing bronchial smooth muscle. Wikipedia reports an elimination half-life of 11 to 16 hours and notes it is less susceptible to metabolism by COMT than catecholamines.
quick.risks: The label lists nervousness, tremor, headache, palpitations and tachycardia, and carries a boxed warning against use for preterm labour after maternal deaths and serious cardiac events. It is prescription-only, and WADA prohibits it except inhaled with a prior therapeutic use exemption.

lead: Terbutaline is a selective beta-2 adrenergic agonist sold as Bricanyl, Brethine and Marex, among other names. It was patented in 1966, entered medical use in 1970 and is indicated for preventing and reversing bronchospasm in people aged 12 and older with asthma, bronchitis and emphysema. [3][4]
It has also been used off-label to delay preterm labour, which led the FDA in 2011 to add a boxed warning on injectable and oral forms. [3][4]
No trials of terbutaline for fat loss or muscle gain were identified in the sources reviewed, and the reviewed encyclopedic sources do not describe such use.
infobox: Prescription-only; WADA-prohibited except inhaled with TUE

paras: Terbutaline is a reliever for asthma and bronchospasm; inhaled forms work within about 15 minutes. [3][4] Several classic asthma trials used it as the comparison beta-2 agonist against inhaled budesonide. [1][2]
Off-label, it has been used as a tocolytic to delay preterm labour for up to 48 hours. [4]

The US label lists effects similar to other sympathomimetic amines; the Grokipedia summary of the label gives nervousness, tremor, headache, palpitations and tachycardia as the most common. [3][5] Wikipedia lists tachycardia, anxiety, tremor, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia and rarely pulmonary edema. [4]

In February 2011 the FDA required a boxed warning that injectable terbutaline should not be used for preterm labour beyond 48 to 72 hours and oral terbutaline not at all, citing serious maternal heart problems and death. [3][4]
Its tertiary butyl group increases beta-2 selectivity, and it lacks the 4-hydroxy group that makes catecholamines susceptible to COMT. About 90% is excreted in urine. [4]
The World Anti-Doping Agency prohibits terbutaline like all beta-2 agonists, except when inhaled with a therapeutic use exemption obtained in advance. [4]

No studies found for appearance uses such as fat loss or muscle gain. Registered and published trials concern asthma, COPD exacerbations and obstetric uses such as tocolysis for fetal distress. [1][2][6][7]

timeline.event: FDA requires a boxed warning against preterm-labour use. [4]
